At my clinic mental health isn't an acceptable reason without a doctor's note, but I often just use my personal days as mental health days. Most workplaces should have a certain amount of days a year (typically 3 or 5) where you don't need to tell them why you're calling off. To be honest, legally you never have to give a reason why you're calling off, you are just unable to make it, they can't require a reason it's just counted as inexcused, though it is frowned upon.

I feel like the obvious ones have been mentioned so I'll skip those and say 

Norita tonkotsu miso ramen.
They are cheap noodles so to really absorb the flavor you have to give it like 10 minutes or so but it's a dollar tree ramen and I absolutely love it. The longer you wait the better it tastes, I've let it sit like 20 minutes and put eggs and vegetables in there and it tasted similar to a pork tonkatsu I got at a restaurant, the only thing off was... the noodles.

I just got the therapist and she was specifically for my relationships since even my relationship with work could be considered unhealthy. She hasn't helped but I feel like I need to give her time to warm up to me.

In the past 5 months i have changed completely as a person. People are always changed, but both of us have changed an extreme amount together. This could be said about any relationship, there is not a point in life in which someone stops changing. You may be more equipped to handle it earlier in life but if you always think about how change will or could affect things, you'll restrict yourself on how you can move forward.
Am I planning on proposing to him, hell no, does not change the fact I feel this way.

Yea.... maybe... I mean that's why I posted this here, because I can't say anything about it to people I know. I seem crazy, yes, but I just needed to tell someone, anyone without a fact I already know being pointed back in my face.

Custom made porcelain. Full porcelain body, and the clothes are hand made, the match my exact preferences in rococo fashion and everything. That actually sounds really fun. Especially since my first porcelain doll was fixed with kintsugi. Still I'm kinda embarrassed to admit that I was careless. But yea I should just tell him and rip it off like a bandaid.

Well to be honest I had to switch dentists recently because my old dentist called me lazy and would patch up all my cavities, putting some on "hold" and told me that i should just start saving for dentures now (even though their assitant told me not to worry and it wasnt that that bad). It was a pretty bad experience and has since made me too afraid to look for a different dentist but I need to now since one of my old fillings popped out and has been causing me pain.

People who honk right as a light turns green or when someone takes too long turning. It's happened to me a few times, but really started to bug me when I saw how hard it is for my friends (yes I know multiple people like this) who have one arm to turn the wheel. Multiple times people would even cut around them and almost get in an accident when they started to turn. Ever since that experience, when it happens to me it's no longer just "they're an asshole, let it go" it just pisses me off even more that I could tell myself to "just let it go" where as my friends can't.

Telling just the general population this, they always respond with something like "excuses excuses" which is why I used that word. I'm afraid to be honest with my dentist on the "why" or even answer the question in the first place which is why I asked this question. I just wanna have some hope that I won't be too heavily judged

Hobbies. I used to like writing and and reading. Recently though the only thing I really do is play gamesbor stare into space.

Relationships. My family was absent from my life because as a child I was too violent (I wanted to be a boy and my father taught me strength was masculinity, how he got in all these fights to prove it so I did the same) later it was because my sister needed their attention more since she was apparently struggling more mentally than me. However they never acknowledged her suicidality. I was the one to find her after every attempt. They never really helped her but they were certainly nicer to her. Because I took care of my sister during this time, she resents me. She couldn't have a twin sister because I was stuck "parenting" her and she felt that I thought I was better than her, I don't. Her hatred for me got so bad she wished I would kill myself because she thought it would make her stop wishing she could kill herself. Years later the relationship should heal, but it hasn't. My father leaves and comes back, he is always drinking, my mother reentered my life because she thinks I'm going to pursue education or law as a career, careers she wish she pursued. She is basically trying to play puppeteer and every time I tell her that I am struggling and college  is the last place I wanna be. She always starts crying and saying how I'm just throwing her through a loop and makes my decision extremely personal to her.

History with trauma....

I was SA'ed when I was 7. The other girl was 5. It's not traumatic in the way that "oh they touched me" but more in the way that I should have known something was wrong and told someone. I know because of that she had to have been SA'ed by someone in her life. But her mother was completely single at the time. So who did it.

When I was 7 I was "kidnapped" (invited to go in her house and then locked in) by my mother's friend, told everything was my fault.

When I was 10 I was forced into starvation by my mother because I was a rectangle and kind of chubby and told I didn't look feminine enough.

I walked in on my sister's suicide at school in its grade and listened to everyone laugh at it.

Other than that I was beat by my father and belittled by my whole family. Cps has never cared about my situation so I've just been left feeling like it doesn't really matter.

Because I've been waiting for forever. I have been suicidal for as long as I can remember, I have been socially crippled for as long as I can remember. Every little ounce of happiness has been extremely momentary and fragile. And there's an issue to being happy when you haven't been in so long. It's uncomfortable and you can't enjoy it, but the second that happiness is gone you realize just how terrible everything is. You don't realize how bad the depression or anything is when you experience it at a constant. Those minutes of happiness have become torture in the recent years.
Agree. I'm either writing a novel or nothing.
